reasons: Lake identity is Brewer v. Williams, U.S. Supreme Court, year 1977.
Lake citations include official 430 U.S. 387, parallels 97 S. Ct. 1232 and 51 L. Ed. 2d 424, and vendor cite 1977 U.S. LEXIS 64.
The opinion states that Detective Leaming delivered the "Christian burial speech" and that the state courts treated it as tantamount to interrogation.
The opinion states Leaming "deliberately and designedly set out to elicit information" and "purposely sought" incriminating information while Williams was isolated from counsel.
The opinion affirms on the Sixth Amendment right-to-counsel ground and rejects waiver on this record.
residual_risks: The holding field is visibly truncated with an ellipsis, but the proposition stated before the ellipsis is supported.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use Brewer's own phrasing: the speech was "tantamount to interrogation" and was deliberate elicitation after adversary proceedings had commenced.

reasons: The opinion frames the dispositive issue as deprivation of the Sixth and Fourteenth Amendment right to assistance of counsel.
The opinion applies Massiah after adversary proceedings had commenced and treats Brewer as a refinement/application of the right-to-counsel deliberate-elicitation rule.
The case is significant enough for a key home role because the Court affirms habeas relief on that constitutional ground.
Lake identity lists court_level as scotus and court as U.S. Supreme Court, supporting the SCOTUS binding-weight label.
